How does one censor censorship? How does it work?

It's still censorship. And it starts a very slippery slope anytime you start making exceptions. Let's say I'm a little Reddit mod and I want to censor people who are saying nasty things, but I have to obey our rule. How can I bend it to fit what I want? It's actually really easy with a little bit of mental gymnastics:

Mental Gymnastics in Action

  • I can only ban people who are censoring others.
  • I want to ban people saying nasty things.
  • People saying nasty things deters others from speaking their minds.
  • Since these people cannot speak their minds, they are being censored.
  • Therefore these people saying nasty things are actually censoring other people.
  • I can ban people saying nasty things.

And now I've justified banning people saying nasty things by using nothing but one well intentioned exception to no censorship. No, censorship is censorship no matter the reason. And as always it's most important to not censor the people you want to censor. Censorship is not used against popular speech or popular actors - it's used against unpopular actors who say and/or do unpopular things. It's like our increasingly broken democracies. Our representatives love to speak to no end of the power and utility of democracy until a vote doesn't go how they like or they can't get people to want to vote for something, in which case it's time to start doing everything possible to undermine the system. If we really stand for no censorship then that certainly means there should be plenty of people doing and saying things you vehemently disagree with.
